headline: Anthropic's threat report and the PaperCut swarm show attackers handing whole intrusion workflows to commercial AI models, while maximum-severity flaws in GitLab, Cisco, and JFrog Artifactory draw exploitation within hours of disclosure.

emerging_trends.text: A Russian-speaking operator built a working PaperCut exploit in a private lab, then turned AI agents loose to break into 395 organizations across 48 countries, collapsing the gap between disclosure and mass compromise.
emerging_trends.topic_title: PaperCut Ships Maintenance Releases After AI-Agent Campaign

emerging_trends.text: Attackers spent the week inside the software factory itself, chaining JFrog Artifactory flaws to plant a Rust backdoor and probing GitLab's maximum-severity file-read bug a day after GitLab published it.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Intruders Backdoor Unpatched JFrog Artifactory Servers

emerging_trends.text: Huntress found criminals hosting malware lures inside weaponized Claude Artifacts and shared AI conversations while Anthropic reported seven Chinese labs draining its models through illicit distillation, which makes the AI platform both the weapon and the prize.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Attackers Turn AI Platforms Into Delivery Infrastructure

topics.title: Criminals Point Claude at Malware Evasion
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic published the full threat report behind yesterday's disclosure, naming the clusters Generative Threat Groups and covering December 2025 through August 2026: GTG-20006, which aligns with the Russian state-sponsored group Midnight Blizzard, used Claude to rebuild malware each time defenders detected it and ran the campaign against more than 20 government, intelligence, diplomatic, and defense organizations; other groups used the models for weapons design, propaganda, and mass surveillance; criminals breached AI vendor infrastructure and stole a pre-release Claude model; and Anthropic separately disrupted industrial-scale distillation attacks from seven China-based labs, among them Alibaba, Moonshot, DeepSeek, Z.ai, and MiniMax, that pumped its models to extract capabilities into their own.
topics.summary: Attackers now fold commercial models into ordinary espionage and criminal work, using them to mutate malware past detection engines and to write convincing executive impersonations, and they treat the model vendors themselves as targets worth breaching. Finance teams should confirm every payment-detail change through a channel separate from email.

sources.title: Anthropic Says Seven China-Based AI Labs Ran Industrial-Scale Claude Distillation Attacks
Russian State-Sponsored Hackers Use Claude to Rebuild Malware After Detection
Anthropic Says Russian Hackers Used Claude AI to Automate Malware Evasion

topics.title: PaperCut Ships Maintenance Releases After AI-Agent Campaign
topics.latest_developments: PaperCut released maintenance releases 26.0.5, 25.0.13, and 24.1.10 that replace every emergency patch the company had pushed for the two actively exploited flaws, and GreyNoise detailed the attacker's method: a private lab holding a vulnerable copy of PaperCut NG/MF and an Active Directory domain, where the suspected Russian-speaking operator built and tested the exploit before handing the break-ins to AI agents that reached at least 440 instances at 395 organizations in 48 countries; Dark Reading traced the agents through the whole kill chain, from staging the lab to reconnaissance, lateral movement, and exfiltration.
topics.summary: PaperCut NG/MF runs print management for schools, universities, and enterprises worldwide, and the exploited pair chains an authentication bypass with remote code execution. Administrators should move straight to 26.0.5, 25.0.13, or 24.1.10 and hunt for unfamiliar accounts and outbound connections to 45.142.193.132.

topics.title: GitLab and Check Point Ship Critical Patches
topics.latest_developments: Attackers began probing GitLab's CVE-2026-85706 in the wild within hours of the September 10, 2026 disclosure, a 10.0-rated path traversal bug in the repository commits API that lets an unauthenticated user read any file on the GitLab server; Check Point assigned CVE-2026-85102 and CVE-2026-85103 to the two critical VPN certificate handling flaws in its Security Gateways and Security Management products that yield remote code execution.
topics.summary: GitLab holds the source code and continuous integration pipelines of the companies that run it, and Check Point gateways terminate corporate VPN traffic, so both sit where one flaw opens everything behind it. Administrators should apply each vendor's fix immediately.

topics.title: Surfshark Test Server and Trezor Phishing Fallout
topics.latest_developments: Surfshark disclosed that a configuration error left one of its internal test servers facing the internet and hackers reached the engineering material, internal configurations, and proxy servers on it; Trezor put numbers on the phishing that followed the breach at its email provider Brevo, counting 347,000 addresses targeted and 2,500 customers who clicked the malicious link, and SecurityWeek reported that the same Brevo access also pushed phishing to users of BitBox and CoinTracking; IDScan confirmed that hackers reached customer data in its cloud platform.
topics.summary: IDScan, the Louisiana identity verification firm that runs ID checks for car rental companies, retailers, and cannabis dispensaries, posted its acknowledgment on September 4, 2026 without naming a victim count, days after researchers tied it to a dark-web trove of 153 million driver's license scans. Trezor customers should treat any email asking for a recovery seed as theft in progress.

topics.summary: Treasury wants banks to feed it more detail on what happens to defrauded customers, the raw material for sanctions and seizures against the Southeast Asian and African compounds. Banks should route scam cases into suspicious activity reports rather than closing them as ordinary fraud.

topics.title: Cisco Firewall Flaws Deliver Qilin Ransomware
topics.latest_developments: Sophos identified the malware riding one of the intrusion clusters as Cyclops Blink, the modular implant Russia's Sandworm group deployed against network devices years ago, now rebuilt with new capabilities and aimed at Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center appliances; Cisco Talos had already named the payoff behind the three clusters exploiting CVE-2026-20079, the 10.0-rated authentication bypass in the Secure Firewall Management Center web interface, and CVE-2026-20316, which steal credentials and then deploy Qilin ransomware.
topics.summary: Secure Firewall Management Center sets policy for Cisco firewalls, so an unauthenticated bypass there hands an attacker the perimeter and the credentials the appliance holds. CISA gave federal civilian agencies until September 12, 2026 to patch; every other operator should install Cisco's fixes and rotate stored credentials now.

topics.title: Intruders Backdoor Unpatched JFrog Artifactory Servers
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer identified the payload the intruders plant on self-hosted Artifactory servers as a Rust backdoor, reached by chaining a critical authentication bypass with a high-severity flaw to gain administrative privileges; Wiz dated the attacks from August 15 through September 8, 2026 and found they reached only the servers whose operators had skipped JFrog's earlier fixes, and CISA on September 10, 2026 added two MikroTik RouterOS bugs already under exploitation, CVE-2026-67277 and CVE-2026-86060, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
topics.summary: Artifactory holds the packages that software build pipelines pull from, so a backdoor there reaches every application a company ships. Operators of self-hosted Artifactory should apply JFrog's fixes, audit administrator accounts, and inspect stored artifacts for tampering.

sources.title: Attackers Chain JFrog Artifactory Flaws to Gain Admin Control and Plant Backdoors

topics.title: Attackers Turn AI Platforms Into Delivery Infrastructure
topics.latest_developments: Huntress documented criminals hosting malware lures inside weaponized Claude Artifacts, shared AI chat transcripts, and sponsored search results, poisoning search results for people looking for AI tools and pushing ClickFix-style prompts; the SANS Internet Storm Center traced an attacker running a semi-autonomous coding agent that hunts poorly secured large language model resale gateways, farms accounts and exploits ordinary web flaws to take API access, validates the capacity, and aggregates the stolen inference behind a gateway of their own; and Ars Technica reported ClickFix infections spreading on both Windows and macOS.
topics.summary: ClickFix tells a victim to paste a command into a terminal or Run dialog to fix a fake error, and the lure now arrives dressed as legitimate AI content on platforms users already trust. Tell staff to treat any web page that asks them to paste a command as an attack, and check whether your own LLM gateways demand authentication.

sources.title: How Threat Actors Are Turning Trusted AI Platforms Into an Attack Surface
ClickFix attacks infecting PCs and Macs are going viral

topics.title: UNC3569 Rides Sogou Input Method to GRAYRABBIT
topics.latest_developments: Gen Digital published research on September 10, 2026 showing that the China-linked group UNC3569 exploited a flaw in Sogou Input Method, the Tencent-owned tool that ranks among the most widely used ways to type Chinese characters on Windows, starting each intrusion with a crafted link and finishing with a backdoor called GRAYRABBIT that carries the logged-in user's full rights.
topics.summary: Sogou Input Method sits on millions of Windows desktops and loads into every application that accepts typing, which makes it an unusually quiet foothold. Organizations with Chinese-language users should inventory Sogou installations and update them.

sources.title: China-Linked UNC3569 Exploited Sogou Input Method Flaw to Deploy GRAYRABBIT Backdoor

topics.title: A Few Dollars Kicks a Stranger's Phone Off the Network
topics.latest_developments: Researchers at Michigan State University and three partner schools bought a Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7, copied the identification number printed on the sealed box, reported the handset to its carrier as lost, and then found that the phone, still new and sitting on a lab bench, refused to connect, one of six weaknesses they found in how carriers process lost-phone reports.
topics.summary: Anyone who reads a handset's identifier off a box, a receipt, or a repair ticket can knock that phone off the cellular network for a few dollars, with no access to the device or the account. Carriers hold the fix: verify that whoever reports a loss actually controls the line.

reading.summary: Newport answers Anthropic employees who said publicly that the systems they build could kill billions, arguing that superintelligence remains a story people tell themselves. reading.summary: Ben Thompson reads Apple's latest launch as another demonstration of what integrating hardware and software buys the company. He names Apple's belief in the primacy of apps as its largest blind spot in an AI era that favors an intelligent personal hub.
